introHeading: The roaming booth for The Bronx's tightest and busiest venues
introParas: There's no booth to place, which means there's no footprint to negotiate — the roaming photo booth is an attendant carrying a handheld, lit capture system through your event, taking photos wherever guests happen to be standing. It's the answer for the kind of Bronx venue where floor space is already committed: a Mott Haven gallery opening where the art is the point, a Country Club backyard party with a tent barely covering the tables, a Riverdale estate reception where the ceremony and cocktail hour share the same lawn.

Sessions take under a minute. The attendant approaches a group, they pick stills, GIFs or boomerangs, and the photo lands on their phone by text or email before they've sat back down. Because there's no line to form, it works especially well at cocktail hours and seated dinners — the kind of moment a static booth in another room simply misses. At larger Bronx weddings, especially the two-hundred-guest receptions common at Throggs Neck's waterfront halls, we usually recommend pairing the roamer with a mirror or glam booth: the static booth anchors one part of the room and draws a crowd, while the roamer covers the seated tables and the guests who stepped outside near Pelham Bay Park and would never have queued.

It's a strong fit for galas, corporate mixers and any venue where a static booth's 8ft x 8ft footprint just isn't available. There's no travel fee anywhere in The Bronx, so the quote you get from your venue ZIP code is the number on the invoice.

faqHeading: Roaming Photo Booth in The Bronx — FAQ

faqs.q: How much space does the roaming booth need?
faqs.a: None. That's the point of it. There's no footprint to plan around, no power run and no backdrop, which makes it the answer for Bronx venues where every square foot is already spoken for — a gallery opening in Mott Haven or a packed backyard party in Country Club.

faqs.q: Does the roaming booth need power at the venue?
faqs.a: No. The handheld capture system runs on its own power, so there's no dedicated outlet to plan for — one less thing to coordinate at a tight Bronx venue.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee anywhere in The Bronx?
faqs.a: No. There's no travel fee anywhere in The Bronx. We quote it from your venue ZIP code before you book so there's nothing to discover on the invoice afterward.

faqs.q: Should we pair the roaming booth with a static booth for a Bronx wedding?
faqs.a: It's common for weddings over about 150 guests, which is routine at Throggs Neck's bigger halls. The mirror or glam booth anchors one part of the room and draws a crowd, while the roamer covers the seated tables and the guests outside who would never have queued.

faqs.q: What Bronx venues is the roaming booth best suited for?
faqs.a: Gallery and loft spaces in Mott Haven, estate lawns in Riverdale, and backyard parties in Country Club — anywhere there simply isn't 8ft x 8ft to spare for a static booth.

faqs.q: Does the roaming booth print photos?
faqs.a: The roamer is a digital-first experience — photos go straight to guests' phones by text or email. If you want prints as well, we pair it with a static booth and printer station.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the roaming booth rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant carries the capture system through the room for the full length of your rental, working the crowd and keeping sessions moving without any help from your own team.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for our Bronx venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy. If your Bronx venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we'll send it over.

faqs.q: Can the roamer cover an outdoor Riverdale or Pelham Bay event?
faqs.a: Yes — since there's no booth structure or backdrop to protect from weather, the roamer is one of the easiest formats to run outdoors. The attendant just needs a charged device and a safe, dry path to walk, so a Riverdale lawn ceremony or a Pelham Bay Park-adjacent reception works well.
